data.narrative:
QuEra Computing is a Series B quantum computing company that has raised $230M to date. The valuation analysis is informed by a peer universe of 11 comparable companies—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum and Infleqtion—though direct same-stage comparables within the quantum computing sector remain sparse.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($230M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series B-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $437M. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable; while 6 quantum computing peers exist in the dataset, insufficient granularity within same-stage or adjacent-stage cohorts (fewer than 3 datapoints per filter) would introduce misleading anchoring. Reliance on all-sector medians was therefore rejected.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $371M to $503M, with a median point of $437M. This range reflects modest sensitivity bounds around the single applicable method rather than convergence across multiple independent techniques. Key uncertainties include the lack of directly comparable Series B quantum hardware valuations, which limits confidence in the step-up multiplier, and the early-stage nature of the sector itself, where traditional stage-progression patterns may not yet be predictive. Users should treat this range as illustrative pending acquisition of richer peer-stage data or customer-traction metrics.
